newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korean conglomerates see strong '97 export growth.
newsitem.headline: Korean conglomerates see strong '97 export growth.

text.p: South Korea's 30 top conglomerates expect their exports to post double-digit growth next year, picking up from this year's slump, the Federation of Korean Industries said on Tuesday.

A recent survey found the 30 groups, known as "chaebols", had forecast their exports to rise by 15 percent to $177 billion in 1997 from an estimated $153 billion this year, a federation statement said.

It said improvements in technology and quality, a rise in demand from developing and industrialised nations, a stable foreign exchange rate and keener competitiveness were behind the expected export growth.
"Exports are likely to recover next year," said Lee Geun-tae, economist at LG Economic Research Institute. "However, that doesn't mean it's going into full swing."
"I think unit prices of South Korea's major export products have seen their bottom and will stabilise next year," said Lee Chul-soon, research fellow at Daewoo Economic Research Institute.
The survey also showed that conglomerates expected exports to grow a mere nine percent in 1996 compared with an earlier forecast of 21 percent growth.
In 1995, exports by the 30 chaebols rose 36.4 percent to $141 billion.
The statement attributed the slump in this year's exports to sharp falls in prices of semiconductors, steel and petrochemicals.
The international spot price for a 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chip, the most widely used memory chip, has fallen to between $7 and $8 from around $50 late last year.
The depreciation of the yen against the dollar was also cited as a major factor, making Japanese products more competitive.
